overall: The AG found the Freetown Planning Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law on any alleged ground: the agenda topic was specific enough, the waiver discussion flowed from it, no attachments were required, and the chair could limit public comment.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the March 21 notice topic for a site plan review and special permit was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: We are satisfied that the topic as listed for the site plan at 52 County Road was sufficient to reasonably advise the public of the issues to be discussed at the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed site plan waivers that were not separately listed on the March 21 notice.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, we find that the discussions about the waivers for the site plan naturally flowed from the Board’s consideration of the posted agenda topic and therefore the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by not separately listing this as a topic on the notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to post the site plan, special permit and waiver documents tied to a topic on the March 21 notice.
allegations.key_passage: the Board was not required to include attachments pertaining to topics listed on the notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board did not allow further public participation at the March 21 meeting after discussing the site plan and waivers.
allegations.key_passage: Because it is within the Chair’s discretion to limit public participation during a meeting, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law when the Chair did not allow for further public participation during the March 21 meeting.
